description: The same rejection through the OTHER receiver: SDTYYYYI arrives as 'abcd' and the store at :313-315 goes through WS-NUM-9999 PIC 9999, so :315 writes '0000' back. Four digits rather than two, which is why the two receivers are separate statements in the source and separate cases here. '0000' satisfies the IS NUMERIC test at :347, so that edit passes too, and the composed '0000-07-01' is rejected by CSUTLDTC at :392 with message number 2521 (FC-YEAR-IN-ERA-ZERO) - again not the tolerated '2513', so :400 reports 'Start Date - Not a valid date...' with the cursor on SDTMML rather than on the year the operator actually got wrong. That misdirection is the program's, and it is preserved. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by reading app/cbl/CORPT00C.cbl, its copybooks, app/bms/CORPT00.bms and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD - never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible in this environment (risk R-A). Java has no transient data queue, so EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD QUEUE('JOBS') at :517 is reproduced through an explicit job-submission port; the eighty-byte content is identical and the dataset key JOBS names the TDQUEUE(JOBS) that app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:499-505 defines as RECORDSIZE(80) RECORDFORMAT(FIXED) BLOCKFORMAT(UNBLOCKED) DISPOSITION(MOD).
